title: 6.9.13 Check: Grids and tile maps
description: Seven multiple-choice questions on rows and columns, pixels and cells, the offset, bounds and level.delete(). Checked instantly.

questions.question: `map` is an array of strings, one string per row. What does `map[2][5]` give you?
options: The whole of row 2
The pixel position of that tile
The letter in row 2, column 5
The letter in column 2, row 5
questions.explanation: The first index picks the row (a string), the second picks a letter in that row. Read it left to right: row, then column.

questions.question: A lit cell must go dark when it is clicked. What do you change?
options: The colour of the rectangle that is on screen
The value in the grid; the next draw shows it
Nothing yet; the screen has to be cleared first
The size of `CELL`
questions.explanation: The grid is the truth and the screen is a picture drawn from it every frame. Change the data and the picture follows.

questions.question: `TILE` is 40. Which pixel x is the centre of column 3?
questions.explanation: Column 3 starts at 3 * 40 = 120, and the centre is half a tile further: 120 + 20 = 140.

questions.question: `TILE` is 40 and the mouse is at x = 150. Which column is it over, and how do you get it?
options: Column 4, from `round(150 / 40)`
Column 3.75, from `150 / 40`
Column 150, since x is already a column
Column 3, from `floor(150 / 40)`
questions.explanation: 150 / 40 is 3.75. `floor` cuts off the 0.75 and leaves 3, the column the pixel is inside. `round` would say 4, which is the next tile.

questions.question: The wall starts `TOP` = 60 pixels down and each brick is `BH` = 20 tall. A click lands at y = 100. Which row is that?
options: Row 2
Row 5
Row 1
Row 4
questions.explanation: Take the 60 off first: 100 - 60 = 40, and 40 / 20 = 2. Dividing 100 by 20 without taking `TOP` off gives 5, which is row 5 of a wall that starts at the top.

questions.question: The grid has 8 rows (0 to 7) and a words strip under it. A click lands in the strip, so `floor(y / CELL)` is 8. What happens if the code goes straight to `grid[r][c] = ...`?
options: Nothing happens: JavaScript skips a row that is not there and carries on
The last row, row 7, is flipped instead
`grid[8]` is `undefined`, so reading a cell from it stops the sketch
The grid quietly grows a ninth row to fit the click
questions.explanation: There is no row 8, so `grid[8]` is `undefined` and `undefined` has no cells. That is why every click is checked against the size of the grid first.

questions.question: Why does `loadLevel(n)` call `level.delete()` before it builds the next level with `Tiles`?
options: It puts the player back on the P of the old level
It adds up the score once for every coin left
`Tiles` would refuse to build a second level while the first still exists
The old walls and coins would stay on screen and keep blocking
questions.explanation: `Tiles` only adds sprites. The old level is still there until you delete it, so level 2 would be built on top of level 1.
